metadata.note: The Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway's own founding and construction history, researched from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites in response to a question about adding the AT&SF itself -- this dataset previously only had its famous named passenger trains from 1926 onward (see data/santa_fe_chief.geojson and data/santa_fe_san_diegan.geojson), not the railway's own 1859-1926 emergence as a transcontinental system. Covers the original Atchison-Topeka-Pueblo-Raton Pass mainline (including the colorful 1878-80 Raton Pass race and Royal Gorge War against the Denver & Rio Grande, complete with hired gunmen including Bat Masterson and Doc Holliday); the Raton Pass-Albuquerque-Deming extension that linked with the Southern Pacific in 1881 to form the country's second transcontinental route; the California Southern Railroad subsidiary that gave the Santa Fe its own line to San Diego via Cajon Pass (1880-85); and the Chicago, Santa Fe and California Railway subsidiary that finally gave the road its own line into Chicago (1888). All four features end in 1926, handing off cleanly to the existing named-train files, which use modern Amtrak-sourced geometry for these same corridors. Route geometry here follows the real intermediate towns each railroad's own history describes, but is a simplified handful of waypoints, not surveyed track centerline. Era boundaries follow real corporate-history milestones (line openings, the Raton Pass race, the Deming silver-spike ceremony, subsidiary purchases); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not sourced from real timetables. A fifth feature, the Atlantic and Pacific Railroad (Albuquerque-Flagstaff-Needles, 1880-1926), was added later covering the Santa Fe's separate northern route across Arizona through Flagstaff, in response to a question about why Flagstaff wasn't shown on the map despite having rail by 1882; it also ends in 1926, handing off to the same named-train files. ATCHISON-RATON GEOMETRY REBUILT (2026-08-24): that one feature was a chain of just 9 hand-placed waypoints, and it routed the main line north through Pueblo and back south to Trinidad. The December 1948 Santa Fe Chief timetable settles it -- La Junta to Trinidad is 81.8 miles, a direct run, whereas the drawn Pueblo dogleg was about 220 km against the 132 km the timetable books. Pueblo was reached in 1876 by a line north from La Junta, but the main line to Raton Pass never went that way. The feature is now traced on real track through Emporia, Newton, Hutchinson, Great Bend, Larned, Dodge City, Garden City, Syracuse, Lamar, La Junta, Trinidad and Raton, with each span checked against the timetable's mileposts. The other four features in this file are unchanged and remain simplified waypoint chains.
sources: https://www.streamlinerschedules.com/concourse/track8/chief194812.html (Santa Fe Chief, December 1948 timetable). Mileposts from Chicago, used as the route check for the Atchison-Raton feature: Kansas City 451.1, Emporia 563.2, Newton 636.2, Hutchinson 669.1, Dodge City 789.3, La Junta 991.7, Trinidad 1073.5, Raton 1096.3, Las Vegas 1206.3, Lamy 1270.5, Albuquerque 1338.1. La Junta to Trinidad is therefore 81.8 miles direct -- the figure that rules out the old Pueblo routing.

https://kansasheritage.org/research/rr/santafe.html (construction sequence: the line reached Emporia July 1870, Newton July 17 1871, Hutchinson June 8 1872 and Dodge City September 1872; rather than turning south at Dodge City the AT&SF headed south-west over Raton Pass, drawn by the coal deposits near Trinidad).
Wikipedia, tshaonline.org, legendsofamerica.com, railswest.com, denversrailroads.com, mojavedesert.net (corporate and construction history retained from the earlier version of this layer).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Frequencies and speeds in every era are estimates, not from timetables. No milepost source was found for the original Atchison-Topeka line or for Topeka-Emporia, so those two spans are checked only against crow-flight distance. The four other features in this file -- Raton Pass-Deming, the California Southern, the Chicago, Santa Fe and California, and the Atlantic and Pacific -- keep their earlier geometry and are still simplified waypoint chains rather than traced track, apart from the Atlantic and Pacific which was already traced.
geometry_sources: Atchison-Raton Pass only: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API, shortest-path search over the OSM rail graph between the timetable stations, run twice (plain rail, and with a wide gap stitch) and merged. Legs were validated by SPAN -- the legs between each pair of milepost stations are summed and compared with the booked mileage difference, accepted at 0.85-1.25x -- rather than leg by leg, which on a route with this much curvature misjudges both directions.

Result: 7 of 8 spans traced on real track, 9 points replaced by 276, total 1049 km. Span accuracy against the 1948 mileposts: La Junta-Trinidad 131.6 km against 131.6 booked (1.00x), Dodge City-La Junta 326.3 against 325.7 (1.00x), Emporia-Newton 118.4 against 117.5 (1.01x), Newton-Hutchinson 54.0 against 52.9 (1.02x), Trinidad-Raton over the pass 38.9 against 36.7 (1.06x), Hutchinson-Dodge City 220.2 against 193.4 (1.14x).

One span is still a straight line: Atchison to Topeka, the railroad's original 1872 line. It could not be routed at all -- not on active track, not preferring abandoned corridors, and not with a wide gap stitch in a tight corridor -- because that first stretch of the Santa Fe is gone and OpenStreetMap carries no connected trace of it. It is drawn as a 63 km straight line between the two cities.

Per-span tracing result: XX Atchison -> Topeka: no route vs 62.7km crow -- STRAIGHT LINE used | ok Topeka -> Emporia: 97.7km vs 84.0km crow (1.16x) [rail] | ok Emporia -> Newton: 118.4km vs 117.5km booked (1.01x) [rail] | ok Newton -> Hutchinson: 54.0km vs 52.9km booked (1.02x) [rail] | ok Hutchinson -> Dodge City: 220.2km vs 193.4km booked (1.14x) [rail] via Great Bend, Larned | ok Dodge City -> La Junta: 326.3km vs 325.7km booked (1.00x) [rail] via Garden City, Syracuse, Lamar | ok La Junta -> Trinidad: 131.6km vs 131.6km booked (1.00x) [stitched] | ok Trinidad -> Raton: 38.9km vs 36.7km booked (1.06x) [stitched]
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Chartered as the Atchison and Topeka Railroad Feb 11 1859 by Cyrus K. Holliday, renamed Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe in 1863; ground was broken in Topeka Oct 30 1868, and the first run, Topeka to Wakarusa, came Apr 1 1869. Reached Dodge City by 1872, roughly following the old Santa Fe Trail west. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: In Feb 1878 Santa Fe crews grabbed Raton Pass hours ahead of a rival Denver & Rio Grande survey party; that same year the two roads also raced for the Royal Gorge route to Leadville's silver boom. The Royal Gorge War (1878-80) saw both sides hire gunmen -- including Bat Masterson and Doc Holliday on the Santa Fe's side -- before an 1880 court ruling upheld the Rio Grande's prior claim, leaving the Santa Fe only secondary rights through the gorge and pushing it to focus south through Raton instead. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: The Atlantic and Pacific Railroad, a joint venture of the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe and the St. Louis-San Francisco Railway (the 'Frisco'), began laying track west from Isleta Junction near Albuquerque in July 1880. It reached Winslow, AZ Dec 3 1881; a six-month delay followed in early 1882 while crews bridged Canyon Diablo, before the line reached Williams Sept 1 1882 and Flagstaff later that same year, transforming the small settlement into a rail hub. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
